text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: high tail latency & streaming stalls observed on /v1/stream via hosted-us-west. p99 > SLO. Auto-escalation to infra oncall.

oncall-bot: mike (oncall) tagged. Priority: P1. Runbook: streaming-tail-latency.

mike: ack I'm on it. pulling metrics now. ping me if you see customer impact.

anya: seeing p95 ~220ms, p99 ~1.9s for streaming route over the last 6m. spike started at ~3001234500.

sara: confirming streaming stalls (clients report mid-stream stalls then reconnect). percent_stalling_sessions=3.7% (baseline ~0.2%).

kai: logs show a cluster of long kernels on a few GPUs in pool "prod-lex". possible GPU-side stalls.

mike: can we isolate node set? which boxes are hot?

sara: top offending hosts: gpu-node-07a, gpu-node-07b, gpu-node-12c. metric: hw.ecc.correctable.rate on 07a jumped from ~2/hr -> 120/hr. thermal_temp GPU3 92C on 07b.

jess: running quick dmesg from node-07a ->

jess: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=4321, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12345.679000] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed, device minor number 0
[ 12347.000123] GPU corrected ECC error on GPU 0, CE count=118
[ 12349.111222] thermal: gpu sensor 3 critical temp threshold exceeded
```

mike: that looks like intermittent ECC + thermal. Could be flaky card or cooler. For immediate mitigation we should: 1) stop scheduling new streams to those nodes, 2) drain existing streaming sessions with graceful fallback, 3) route traffic to warm fallback pool, 4) scale up dedicated pool by +4 replicas.

anya: starting traffic reroute: `/infra/reroute --from=prod-lex --exclude-nodes=gpu-node-07a,gpu-node-07b,gpu-node-12c --to=prod-lex-fallback`. will take ~30s to propagate.

mike: good. Also bump fallback model concurrency to reduce queuing: `rbctl set pool prod-lex-fallback --max-concurrency=200`.

sara: rolling out now. watch p95/p99.

(30s pass)

sara: p95 dropped from 220ms -> 150ms, p99 from 1.9s -> 320ms. streaming stalls down to 0.4%. progress.

kai: meanwhile infra telemetry shows node-07a ECC correctable rate still climbing despite drain. suspect hardware is flapping.

mike: mark node-07a for immediate quarantine. set `node-label maintenance=planned` and remove from scheduler.

jess: executed: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-07a && drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 gpu-node-07a`. draining streams gracefully with 60s grace.

cs-rep: I'm pinging the top 3 customers with long-running streams in the last hour. I'll send a short note: "We observed intermittent streaming stalls; we've routed traffic to fallback and are investigating. No token leakage. We'll follow up with ETA for hardware replacement."

mike: good. anyone see any fallback failures or model mismatches?

anya: a handful of sessions rolled back to the smaller model due to memory limits; we're increasing fallback slice memory for those customers with active sessions.

kai: quick low-level check on node temps: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu --format=csv` -> GPU3 on 07b at 94C, GPU0 on 07a stable 72C but CE counts >200.

mike: thermal of 94C is worrying. I want rack-level airflow check, but for live mitigation let's keep node 07b cordoned as well. Is there any sign of host kernel log OOM or page faults?

jess: `dmesg | tail` on 07b shows repeated GPU reset attempts and a few `gpu hung` messages.

jess: ```
[ 12358.000000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=9876, GPFault at 0x123456
[ 12360.500000] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus, retrying initialization
```

mike: that's consistent with flaky hardware. We'll escalate to hardware ops for replacement. In the short term, leave those nodes out of rotation.

sara: current customer impact summary (last 45m): ~14k requests affected; SLO breaches (p99) ~540; streaming stall incidents ~210 sessions with at least one stall. Major tier customers impacted: 2 seats (acct-omega, acct-sparrow) had 5% of their sessions stall.

cs-rep: contacting AMs for acct-omega and acct-sparrow now. I'll post the customer message draft in #customer-commms for review.

mike: timeline so far: 3001234500 - spike begins; 3001234545 - incident-bot pages; 3001234590 - initial reroute initiated; 3001234620 - p99 back to ~320ms; 3001234680 - nodes cordoned/draining.

kai: can we confirm no data-plane corruption? KV-cache prefixes looked intact. No model outputs truncated except the stalls.

mike: okay. I'm going to leave this thread open until hardware ops confirm replacement and we validate stable p99 for 30m. Next actions: 1) hw ops ticket with logs + CE counts (jess), 2) postmortem owner (mike), 3) follow-up customer comms (cs-rep/jess), 4) run deeper evict test on 07a/07b once replacement done.

jess: created hw ticket #HW-9842 and attached dmesg, nvidia-smi snapshots, ECC graphs. assigned to hw-ops oncall. ETA initial triage 45m.

anya: alert: small regression at 3001234660 when we added fallback capacity; p95 increased to 180ms briefly due to warmup. resolved.

cs-rep: acct-omega replied: "thx for the heads up, want an SLA credit estimate" — I'll coordinate after we have final impact numbers.

mike: noted. we should capture per-customer breached request counts. sara, can you produce a per-customer SLO breach extract for the window 3001234500-3001234689?

sara: on it, will post CSV to the incident ticket in ~20m.

kai: operational note: we should add a temporary rule to route new streaming sessions away from any host with CE_rate > 50/hr to avoid future spikes while we triage. Can infra ops add that gate?

mike: yes, infra please add `route-filter: deny if node.ecc.correctable.rate > 50`.

jess: infra ops acked and applied the filter.

(45m pass)

jess: hw-ops updated HW-9842: replacement GPU arriving onsite, plan to swap tomorrow 09:00 PST. In the meantime nodes remain cordoned.

sara: metrics steady: p95 140ms, p99 270ms, stalls 0.3% over last 10m.

mike: leaving the ticket open for follow-up. Drafting short post-incident note. Postmortem owner: mike. Slack follow-up meeting at 3001236000 to decide long-term mitigations (better ECC alerting, thermal thresholds, auto-evict policy).

cs-rep: sent updated message to acct-omega + acct-sparrow with apology + interim mitigation details.

mike: final quick checklist before closing this thread: - hardware ticket created (jess: done) - traffic reroute executed (anya: done) - customers notified (cs-rep: done) - postmortem scheduled (mike: done). If no regressions in the next 30m I'll mark resolved.

oncall-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.

mike: thanks all. good triage and quick reroute. we'll follow up with hardware replacement and improvements to routing gate.

incident-bot: incident closed (mitigated) at 3001234689 :white_check_mark:
